title: Thine Honor Rescue, Christ, Our Lord
description: Thine Honor Rescue, Christ, Our Lord in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Johann Heermann wrote these words in German. Matthias Loy's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 275.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thine hon-or res-cue, Christ, our Lord! Hear Zi-on’s sighs and help af-ford; De-stroy the wiles of might-y foes, Who now Thy Word and truth op-pose.

lines: Thine honor rescue, Christ, our Lord!
Hear Zion’s sighs and help afford;
Destroy the wiles of mighty foes,
Who now Thy Word and truth oppose.
Their craft and vaunting pomp is great;
High beat their hearts, with power elate;
Our dearest hopes they but deride,
They deem us nothing in their pride.
Forgive, O Lord, our sins forgive,
Grant us Thy grace and let us live;
Convince Thy foes throughout the land
That godless counsels shall not stand.
Preserve Thy little flock in peace,
Nor let Thy boundless mercy cease;
Let it to all the world appear
That Thy true Church indeed is here.
That Thou art with us loud proclaim,
Who put’st our enemies to shame,
Dost all their haughtiness suppress
And help Thine own in their distress.

licence: Public domain: Johann Heermann died in 1647; Matthias Loy died in 1915.
credits: Words by Johann Heermann (1585–1647), translated by Matthias Loy (1828–1915), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
